reference: An independent Python reference written from a first-principles re-derivation of the rigid liquid-column momentum equation and the pipe/tank continuity equation, solved by a structurally different route: the pair is reduced analytically to a linear first-order ODE for v^2 as a function of the driving head, which is solved in closed form, so the velocity-versus-head curve, the peak velocity and the level at which the column stops are exact algebra with no discretisation at all; the trajectory in time is a single quadrature in the head domain with both square-root endpoint singularities removed exactly by substitution, so there is no time step anywhere in the reference. Verified before use against an implicit stiff integrator (scipy Radau) run on the original two-equation system, against order doubling of its own quadrature, and against published closed forms and asymptotics: the frictionless mass-oscillation period and amplitude, the frozen-head Riccati/tanh solution, Torricelli's law and the Torricelli drain-time law with its leading inertial correction, and Colebrook-White solved to convergence. The page is driven in a real browser through its own permalink state codec and every quantity it reports is graded against that reference. The superseded in-page limit checks are retained in this artifact, relabelled as self-checks, with their acceptance bands rebuilt so that none is a function of the simulated-time input.
reference_citations: Rigid water-column (lumped-inertia) momentum equation (L/g) dV/dt = H - c V|V| together with tank continuity dh/dt = -+ (A_pipe/A_tank) V: E. B. Wylie and V. L. Streeter, Fluid Transients in Systems, Prentice Hall, Englewood Cliffs NJ, 1993, rigid-column chapter; and M. H. Chaudhry, Applied Hydraulic Transients, 3rd ed., Springer, New York, 2014, surge-tank chapter. Re-derived from Newton's second law for the column in section 1 of this file and implemented from that derivation.

Frictionless mass oscillation of a tank-pipe-reservoir system: the level is harmonic about the boundary level at omega = sqrt(g A_pipe/(A_tank L)), period T = 2 pi sqrt(A_tank L/(g A_pipe)), with the column overshooting by exactly its initial head. Classical frictionless surge-tank result (Chaudhry, 3rd ed., surge-tank chapter; Wylie and Streeter, 1993, rigid-column chapter). Used here as the anchor for the terminal time and terminal level of the zero-loss cases.

Riccati/tanh solution of the rigid-column equation at frozen head, v = v_inf tanh(g H t/(L v_inf)) with v_inf = sqrt(2 g H/K_t): obtained in section 1 by integrating (1) with H held constant; the same limit is quoted in the surge-tank and rigid-column literature above.

Torricelli's law v = sqrt(2 g H) for efflux under a head (E. Torricelli, De Motu Gravium Naturaliter Descendentium, 1644), recovered here as the K_t = 1 quasi-steady limit, and its integrated drain-time law t = (2 sqrt(H0)/alpha) sqrt(K_t/(2 g)), whose leading inertial correction is measured in section 3 at 1.19/(beta H0).

C. F. Colebrook, Turbulent flow in pipes, with particular reference to the transition region between the smooth and rough pipe laws, Journal of the Institution of Civil Engineers 11 (1939) 133-156. Solved to convergence (bisection on 1/sqrt(f), residual below 1e-15 relative) to set the Darcy factor of the friction-only case at a stated Reynolds number and relative roughness, rather than picking a round number. Reproduces the published smooth-pipe Moody value 0.0180 at Re = 1e5.

J. G. Verwer, E. J. Spee, J. G. Blom and W. Hundsdorfer, A second-order Rosenbrock method applied to photochemical dispersion problems, SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 20 (1999) 1456-1480 -- the ROS2 scheme, gamma = 1 - 1/sqrt(2), that the corrected page march now uses. Cited for what the tool does, not as a reference for grading it.
provenance_note: Independent second implementation in Python (bench-src/gen_pipe_filling_draining.py, sections 1-3), derived from first principles and solved by closed form plus quadrature in the head domain; no part of the page JavaScript is ported or paraphrased. Run outside the browser; the page is driven separately through its permalink state codec and only its reported outputs are read. Self-verified by 48 checks against published closed forms, published asymptotics, an implicit stiff integrator and quadrature order doubling before any grading. Equation numbering in the cited monographs could not be verified offline, so those two results are cited by edition and chapter subject rather than by equation number; the equations themselves are written out in section 1 and re-derived there. All 253 graded references are recomputed during this run and none reuses a stored or published number: 233 by that implementation, including the four analytic anchors it evaluates itself, and 20 by the page's own retained in-page limit checks, relabelled basis = "self-check" and counted separately.
tolerance: Every driven output is graded at 1e-6 of its own physical scale: the initial driving head H0 = |h0 - h_boundary| for the level and for the driving-head pressure (through rho g H0), the closed-form peak velocity for velocities and for the volume flow (through A_pipe), and the elapsed transient for the time. That band is fixed by two things and by nothing the user can type. First, the page's march holds its own embedded ROS2 error estimate to RTOL = 1e-7 per step, so 1e-6 is ten times the integrator's declared step-control tolerance; a 400-point randomised scan over the whole declared input box put the largest departure from this reference at 5.0e-8, twenty times inside the band. Second, the reference itself contributes nothing at that level: its Gauss-Legendre quadrature moves by less than 1e-9 relative when the order is quadrupled from 80 to 320, and it agrees with an independent Radau integration of the original two-equation system to between 1e-10 and 1e-8. The band is also far below the tool's own printed precision (elapsed 2 dp, level and velocity 3 dp), so the printed answer is the looser of the two constraints everywhere. Cases with no driving head have no scale, and are graded on absolute floors of 1e-9 m, 1e-12 m/s and 1e-12 s. The published anchors carry their own derived bands, stated per case: the frictionless half period and mirror level at 1e-6 relative; Torricelli's velocity at the finite-tank head drop alpha*v*t/(2 H0) plus the march band; the quasi-steady drain-time law at twice its own leading inertial correction 1.19/(beta H0). The invariance group requires the terminal time, level and peak velocity to be IDENTICAL to the last bit across simulated-time windows from 1.05x to 89700x the transient; the band is zero because the corrected march contains no dependence on that input at all.
grading: total counts checks with an acceptance criterion. 233 of them are independent: the page is driven in a browser and every quantity it reports is compared with the Python reference or with a published closed form. The remaining 20 are the superseded in-page limit checks, retained and relabelled as self-checks because they re-evaluate the tool's own relations inside the tool; they are recorded with their original ids, notes and verdicts but do not carry the benchmark claim. The in-page termination-branch and terminal-head rows report the state of the solved case, carry no criterion, and are excluded from the count.

notes: Independent cases drive the shipped page through its own permalink state codec (?s=J<base64>) in headless Chromium and read window.Diagram.record.build(), so the graded numbers are the ones the tool reports, not a re-implementation of them.

Both modes are covered, both terminations (requested horizon and column at rest), the lossless and loss-dominated ends, the stiff short-pipe corner, every declared input limit, and the three no-driving-head branches.

DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED (first run, against the shipped build 2026-09-11.transients-1.8-report). The march nominated its step as tEnd/1200, where tEnd is the simulated-time window -- a display input carrying no physics -- and it marched that step with an explicit two-stage Heun predictor-corrector. Two failures followed from the one line. (1) Every terminal-event answer moved with the window: on one drain case the reported terminal time ran 111.49 s at a window 1.05x the transient, 118.91 s at 20x (+6.7 %), 65.03 s at 100x (-41.7 %) and 9289.77 s at 1e5x, a spread of 8267.89 s on a transient that lasts 111.48 s. (2) Worse, the pair is stiff -- drag relaxes velocity on L/(K_t v) while the level moves on A_tank H/(A_pipe v) -- so for any short pipe with heavy local loss the explicit stage went unstable at the step the window handed it, on inputs well inside the declared ranges and with the window set to the actual duration of the transient. A 50 m2 tank draining 8 m through 1 m of 100 mm pipe with K = 1000 reported a terminal tank level of -274.999 m, a peak pipe velocity of 0 m/s and a drain time of 214.31 s against a true 257172 s: the drain time under-reported by 1200x and the level was 275 m below the tank bottom. The fill branch was worse in kind: filling a tank toward a 7 m source, the tool reported the tank level reaching 98.28 m, fourteen times the source level and physically impossible, with the fill time 813x short. A large tank filled through a small bore reported v_final = 0 and v_peak = 0 -- no flow at all -- where the true pipe velocity is 1.446 m/s. At the declared minimum column length the reported level was -2.41e6 m. No warning was raised in any of these cases. The superseded in-page benchmark could not see any of it: its acceptance band was the solver's own step, omega|h0-hB|dt and (gH/L)dt with dt = tEnd/1200, a tolerance that grows in proportion to the error it exists to catch, and it never ran the finite-tank finite-loss trajectory at all -- only two limiting cases in which the defect is absent. Run against this reference, the shipped build failed 100 of 233 independent checks. FIXED: the march is now ROS2, the L-stable two-stage Rosenbrock method of Verwer, Spee, Blom and Hundsdorfer (1999) with gamma = 1 - 1/sqrt(2), so the stiff drag can never grow; the step is set by the scheme's own embedded first-order error estimate against a tolerance RTOL = 1e-7 fixed on the initial head and velocity scales, i.e. taken from the transient; and tEnd survives only inside min(dt, tEnd - t), which can shorten the last step onto the requested horizon and can never lengthen any step. The terminal stop and the velocity peak are located by bisection inside the step that brackets them, and the plotted history is decimated afterwards so curve resolution costs the answer nothing. MEASURED AFTER THE FIX: the terminal time, terminal level and peak velocity are now bit-for-bit IDENTICAL across simulated-time windows from 1.05x to 89700x the transient -- spread exactly 0.0, not merely small -- and that invariant value agrees with the independent reference to 6.5e-9 relative. All 233 independent checks pass, with the largest residual anywhere at 3.6 % of its band. The page's Python export carried the same stepper and was rebuilt to match; it now reproduces the browser result to the last bit on every case tested.
